incident: Checkout requests are timing out and the edge is returning 5xx.
title: Inventory Service Replica Reduction Causing Overload and Edge 5xx Errors

root_cause.statement: The inventory deployment replicas were reduced from 4 to 1, causing resource contention, health probe failures, and downstream checkout timeouts.

confidence.label: high
confidence.explanation: High: the leading cause is supported by multiple independent sources and nothing strongly contradicts it.

causal_chain.step: Deployment replicas for inventory were scaled down from 4 to 1 via rollout.
The single inventory pod became overloaded, leading to CPU and memory contention, and health/readiness probe failures.
Inventory stock lookups began failing due to timeouts and connection errors, cascading into upstream checkout failures.
The ShopEdgeHigh5xxRate alert fired as checkout requests timed out and failed at the edge.

facts.statement: Edge is experiencing a high 5xx error rate of 76.21%.
The inventory pod has restarted twice.
The inventory deployment replicas were reduced from 4 to 1.

facts.quote: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.1.65:8080/healthz": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
facts.statement: Inventory pod experienced readiness and liveness probe failures due to timeouts.

facts.quote: FATAL:  sorry, too many clients already
facts.statement: Inventory pods failed database connection due to PostgreSQL too many clients error
Inventory pods encountered connection timeout errors when trying to connect to the database

hypotheses.statement: Inventory service replica reduction to 1 and subsequent resource starvation/overload causes probe failures and downstream checkout timeouts.
hypotheses.mechanism: Reducing inventory replicas from 4 to 1 concentrates all incoming load onto a single pod, causing CPU/memory contention, failed health/readiness probes, and widespread 5xx errors on checkout requests that depend on inventory.

hypotheses.statement: Database connection pool exhaustion caused by too many replicas or unreleased connections.
hypotheses.mechanism: When inventory replicas were scaled or restarted, connection attempts overwhelmed the upstream PostgreSQL database connection limit, causing errors and timeouts in inventory stock lookups.

evidence.rationale: Directly shows that the inventory deployment replicas were scaled down from 4 to 1 right before probe failures and high 5xx errors started.

evidence.quote: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.1.65:8080/healthz": context deadline exceeded
evidence.rationale: Demonstrates that the single inventory pod is struggling to respond to health checks under load.

evidence.quote: FATAL:  sorry, too many clients already
evidence.rationale: Direct evidence of database connection exhaustion matching the resource contention symptoms in inventory.

rejected_evidence.reason: quote not found verbatim in the cited observation

alternatives.why_less_likely: Database connection exhaustion was a symptom of container restarts or connection spikes secondary to the overload, rather than an independent database limit breach.

uncertainty: Whether the replica reduction to 1 was intended or an unintended side effect of a script or rollout.
remediation: Scale the inventory deployment replicas back up to at least 4.
Implement HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) to prevent manual single-replica scaling mistakes from causing capacity outages.
